Every entity in this document is modelled from published architectural photography and a 2021 design site plan, not from OSM, not from LiDAR, and not from the ArcGIS survey. Positions are INFERRED: each item names the surveyed polygon it was anchored to (`anchor`), and that anchor is the only measured fact behind it. Nothing here may be read back as a measurement of the campus, quoted as a height, a colour or a position by campus-eighth.js, campus-eighth-furniture.js, the corridor builders, or any gate. It renders and it is labelled; it does not inform. Class rule: docs/js/campus-photo-eighth.js header, and the README's photo-sourced section.

galbraith.label: Galbraith Hall, Revelle College — photo-sourced detail
galbraith.epoch: 2007-2026 (photographs); 02.17.12 (architect's plan sheets); 1965 (fabric); repo Google orthophoto chunk_4_7/chunk_5_7 (0.125 m/px, built 2026-08-04) for the roof and east ground
galbraith.note: INVENTED class. Deems Lewis Martin, 1965; Kevin deFreitas Architects renovation 2013. Every dimension here comes from a dated photograph or from the architect's Second Floor Plan, scaled against the MEASURED ring in campus-3d.json and the MEASURED LiDAR height. Nothing measured reads back from this section.
galbraith.colorNote: Hexes are pixel medians with the lighting condition named. Two are adjusted from the raw sample and say so: pavingBuff is the ucsdmap.jpg median desaturated for that frame's overcast warm cast, and cofferPan/soffitRib sit mid-way between the sunlit-bounce and deep-shade samples because the renderer supplies its own shading. Roof and east-ground hexes are read off the repo orthophoto crops sat_galbraith.png / sat_east_ground.png (midday sun, warm cast) — nadir medians, not shade-corrected.

measured.heightNote: The 2014 drawn surface is FLAT at 23.5-23.9 m under the whole footprint and across the north apron (sampled on a 2 m grid against makeSurfaceSampler), so there is no storey-high step between the north plaza and the ground at the building's south edge, and the survey's earlier reading — LiDAR 16.6 above the lawn, ArcGIS 12.8 above a plaza one storey higher — cannot be what these two numbers are. That flat pad is LOCAL: the same sampler puts a ~26.8 m ridge 8-9 m west of the ring (west.gradeNote), 27.1 m within 25 m to the south (the lawn climbs past z ~503) and ~26.8 m under the east tree band, which is why every ground field in this section is draped over the drawn terrain and every solid seated per-item on it, never hung on a 23.6 level line. On the flat pad the ring stands on, LiDAR 16.6 is simply the roof above grade on all four sides, and this section puts its eaves exactly there, on top of the measured mass, so nothing measured is left standing above the roof. How the 16.6 divides is read off oceanlight-21220.jpg, which is near-orthographic: scaling that elevation so grade-to-roof is 16.6 gives a 5.6 m lower glazed band, a 3.2 m terrace zone, a 4.5 m upper glazed band and a 3.2 m roof edge — two levels of about 7.4 m and a slab of about 1.8, which sums back to 16.6 with no residual. Two glazed bands split by one mid-level balcony is what the north, south and west photographs all show, and a 7.4 m level is corroborated on the north by ad01-entry-before.jpg, where the plaza-level glazing stands about three door-heights tall. LiDAR decides the ground and the top; the photographs decide only how the space between them divides.
measured.conflict: PARTLY RESOLVED by the repo orthophoto (2026): a raised ~29 m central block with a 9x9 skylight grid demonstrably exists, so the 3.8 m ArcGIS/LiDAR delta has a physical owner — 12.8 is plausibly the low deck and 16.6 the highest return over the block or the penthouses. What stays unresolved is HOW HIGH the block stands (no shadow is measurable; its rim reveal is symmetric on all four sides) and which roof object owns the 16.6 maximum. The drawn measured mass extrudes the whole footprint to 16.6, so this section expresses the roofscape as curb-scale relief on that top rather than re-deriving the facade datum — see roof.datumNote. ArcGIS's 3 levels vs 2 expressed elevations is still taken as an internal third level, unbuilt.

grid.datumNote: standoff, roofOut and every facade projection are measured from the GLAZING PLANE, not from the measured ring: 3.4 m is what the photographs read between the glass and the strut line, and it has to stay 3.4 m however far out the glazing itself has to hang to clear the drawn mass.
grid.calibration: The architect's plan gives 10.83 m between pair centres. That number was calibrated against a 45.8 m enclosed block, and it does NOT survive contact with the surveyed 62 m footprint: the measured ring is the wall this section is allowed to hang on, and five pairs at 10.83 m only span 45.8 m of it. So the drawing's SPACING is dropped and its COUNT is kept — five pairs, 2.45 m inside a pair, both of which are independently countable in oceanlight-21220.jpg — spread across the measured face. The measured world decides scale; the photographs decide what is on it.
grid.moduleNote: The coffer module survives that, because it is corroborated twice over: it is the drawing's own pair spacing over eight (10.83 / 8 = 1.354), and it is also the size that puts the 46 coffers counted across the elevation onto the 62 m measured face (62.0 / 46 = 1.348). The two agree to 6 mm. The oversail is six of them, counted in ad01-entry-before.jpg and again in wm-from-below.jpg.
grid.source: ad-plan-L2.jpg, Kevin deFreitas Architects Second Floor Plan, 02.17.12

column.profileNote: Half-widths are the LATHE CIRCUMRADIUS of a four-sided section, so what an elevation actually shows is radius x sqrt(2): a 0.83 head reads as the photographed 1.17 m bracket and the 0.38 waist as a 0.54 m shaft. Not a straight box and not a plain taper: thin at the waist, sweeping out below into a wide flat foot and flaring above into a broad bracket that meets the beam hard. Section is square with the diagonal facing the wall, which is what ad01 and ucsdmap both show.

roofEdge.source: crop-roofedge.jpg (2011) and wm-from-below.jpg (2026) — present in both epochs

facade.wallStandoffNote: Not a style choice. campus-massing.js extrudes the UNIVERSITY'S massing ring, which stands up to 0.799 m outside the OSM ring this section is anchored to. Glazing hung any closer than that disappears inside the drawn box on the east elevation. The standoff is that clearance plus 0.15 m and nothing more.
facade.mullionNote: ESTIMATE, 1.5-1.8 m read off ad01; finer than the coffer module, never equal to it.

entry.beamNote: The two beams ride the middle pair's column lines and carry the 'Galbraith Hall' lettering on their outer fascia. The lettering itself is ABSENT: there is no text mechanism in this renderer and a painted-on rectangle would be worse than nothing.
entry.signNote: The 'Theatre & Dance Department' hanging blade, in both wm-from-below and flickr.

west.gradeNote: The 2014 ground rises 3.2 m from x -8 to a ridge at x -16.5 that runs dead straight for the whole length of the west face. That ridge is what the lava wall in ucsdmap.jpg retains, but it is also exactly the shape a bare-earth classifier leaves along a hedge or a wall line, so nothing here asserts it is topography: the wall is placed at its crest, OUTSIDE the roof, and every solid on this side is seated per-item on the drawn surface rather than on a level.

Interior fitout of every level, including the 417-seat lecture hall the plan sheets describe.

roof.source: sat_galbraith.png — crop of the repo's own Google orthophoto chunk_4_7.jpg (docs/data/textures, source: google, generated 2026-08-04, 0.125 m/px, world mapping in textures/manifest.json). Positions read off it are +-0.5 m. Per CLAUDE.md satellite imagery is a build-time measurement source only.
roof.datumNote: NO DOUBLE-COUNTING of the 3.8 m. LiDAR 16.6 is a MAXIMUM return, and campus-massing.js draws the measured box to that height over the WHOLE footprint — so the visible box top already stands at the highest real point of this roof. The real low deck sits [estimated] 1.5-2.5 m below it and is buried inside the drawn mass; nothing can be drawn under the box top. Everything here therefore seats ON the drawn box top (the structure it stands on) and rises only curb-scale above it: skylight curbs 0.18 m, block rim 0.12 m, penthouse/mech expression 0.28-0.35 m. Plan positions and pitches are SOURCED; the expression heights are [estimated] and deliberately suppressed so nothing stands a storey above the LiDAR maximum.

block.heightNote: [estimated] 1.5-2.5 m above the true low deck (inventory + the 2012 interior photo); 2.0 m carried as the declared middle. NOT drawn as 2 m of box — see datumNote.
block.revealNote: A dark reveal/gutter 0.5-1.0 m wide rings the block on all four sides in the orthophoto; symmetric, so it is a reveal and not a cast shadow.

skylights.pitchNote: The orthophoto measures a 2.75 m pitch (sigma ~0.05 m); 2 coffer modules is 2.708 m. They agree to under 5 cm per bay, and this building solves on one grid or it is wrong, so the pitch is DERIVED as 2 x grid.module and the raw measurement is recorded here. Field centred on the sourced block rectangle (its centre sits 0.8 m west and 3.6 m north of the ring centroid — the block itself is not quite central and the field follows it). The squares read WHITE from above: white-capped curbs, not dark glass.

roof.penthouseNote: Two stair/lift penthouses projecting north from the block and one large one projecting south; the south one wears a pale seamed metal roof in the orthophoto. z0 433.0 < the ring's 428.9 + 4, i.e. the north pair sit just inside the north edge. Expression height 0.35 m [estimated] — see datumNote.
roof.mechNote: Six dark-walled service enclosures with pale equipment inside, on the low deck. Expression height 0.28 m walls + 0.34 m equipment [estimated] — see datumNote.

east.source: sat_east_ground.png — repo Google orthophoto (chunk_4_7 + chunk_5_7, source: google, generated 2026-08-04), world x 40..110, z 420..505. The building's east edge measures x ~54.7 against the ring's 54.6.

east.walkNote: ~3.1 m pale tan unit-paver / scored-concrete walk running the full north-south length; a fine banded texture is visible. Band pitch 0.45 m [estimated] off the visible banding.
east.footPadNote: A row of pale ~1.0-1.4 m squares along the building side of the walk at ~11-12 m spacing, read as the colonnade column feet showing past the roof edge. east.dgNote: Broad decomposed-granite band under the mature tree canopies out to x~89; the trees themselves stay the measured tree layer's business. east.lawnNote: South-east lawn patch; its shrub masses and the low diagonal wall/step stay absent.
east.constructionNote: EPOCH LIMIT: beyond x ~90 the orthophoto shows active construction — disturbed earth, plant, a temporary haul road, a large white-roofed structure. That ground is in flux and is left UNBUILT.

treeOverrides.note: Photo-layer re-skin of measured LiDAR trunks whose rendered blob crowns would pierce the oversail roof slab. Each item is a row copied VERBATIM from campus-lidar.json trees ([x, z, h, r] as key x,z); the trunk stays measured — position, height and spread are not this section's to move. Only the RENDERED canopy changes: it is pruned below the soffit plane, the way the real understorey tree under the NE oversail corner is kept. That canopy shaping is INVENTED (no photograph resolves this one tree against the slab); its species tint comes from the same campus-species table the measured blob renderer uses, so no new colour enters this file, and nothing measured may read from this block.
treeOverrides.wiringNote: campus-walk.js and campus-scooter.js must union these keys into the createTrees skipKeys set alongside plaza.treeOverrides.skipMeasuredKeys, or the measured blob renderer draws the same stem a second time, through the slab.

items.why: stands 0.5-1.5 m outside the measured ring but fully under the 12.5 m NE roof oversail; its measured 18.3 m top rises past the soffit and the blob crown punched through the slab (visual audit 2026-08-17, az045-high/roof nadir).

plaza.label: Revelle Plaza landscape — trees, ground features and furniture of Zone 1 (the ground between Keeling, York, Argo, Blake and Galbraith)
plaza.epoch: Photographs 2006-2026 decide what exists and how it looks; the georeferenced satellite plan (Google chunks, fetched 2026-08-03) decides plan positions; LiDAR 2014 decides every re-skinned trunk's position, height and crown radius. The coral tree post-dates the LiDAR (planted Feb 2014) and is the one tree here with no measured trunk.
plaza.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail per README. Everything here is modelled off dated photographs and the plan-only satellite read in scratchpad/research/zone1-plaza-landscape.md. Nothing measured may ever read from this section. The treeOverrides re-skin measured LiDAR trunks by position key: heights and crown radii are copied VERBATIM from docs/data/campus-lidar.json (whose r is clamped at 7.5 m and h at 30 m — floors, not measurements). No colour here is sampled from raw satellite pixels. NO PALMS: twelve palm taxa are on the campus list and zero appear in any Zone 1 photograph, so none are built.

treeOverrides.note: Position-keyed re-skins of measured LiDAR trunks (key = 'x,z' exactly as in docs/data/campus-lidar.json trees). This module builds the ultra models; MAIN MUST SKIP the default blob rendering for every key in skipMeasuredKeys or each tree draws twice. Species verdicts are photo-sourced (zone1-plaza-landscape.md §1): the York belt is Torrey pine (the h>=16 heuristic mislabels it eucalyptus), the plaza/Argo broadleafs are ficus, eucalyptus only east of York and on the Keeling west road. Groups E-north and G stay generic blobs — per-tree confidence is too low to re-skin them. The trunk at 55.9,427.4 is re-skinned by the galbraith section instead (its canopy must clear the oversail slab), so it is not in this roster.

pines.source: Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012), Revelle_Plaza_Path,_UCSD.jpg (2011); Pinus torreyana on the official campus species list. Clear bole 55-65% of height, open irregular candelabra crown reading ~40-50% sky.

eucalyptus.source: Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012) — the grove edge east of York (group B), plus the tall road-frontage trees on the Keeling west road (group F, h>=14; keeling-inventory.md corroborates).

coral.tag: [estimated] size — a 5 m nursery specimen in 2014 grown to a 12-year irrigated coral tree; species unresolved among three Erythrina on the campus list, so it is generic and unflowered

lamp.source: Revelle_Plaza__UCSD.JPG (2011), Revelle_Plaza_Path,_UCSD.jpg (2011), Revelle_Plaza.jpg (2006) — three frames agree; scaled off the published 54-inch banner. grid.bayNote: ~30-31 bays over the full south elevation [measured, vmarch-bradley_VMA_UCSDBlake_67.jpg, near-orthographic] — foreshortening-immune. Module = measured face length / 30 = 1.25 m. The inventory's absolute 1.88 m bay was read at the assumed anchor against a 58 m elevation the LiDAR ring draws at 37.5 m; counts win. The sibling DIFFERENCE from Argo survives in what fills the bay — a large glazed panel at 0.85 of the bay against Argo's 0.66 narrow window — and in the storey counts: 2 fin storeys plus penthouse against Argo's 5. CONFLICT declared: the inventory's anchor-immune bay:floor ratio 0.618 (vs Argo's 0.435, called the single most important difference between the two buildings) times 30 bays and the storey implies a ~67 m elevation against the 37.5 m drawn ring — an unresolvable count-vs-ratio source conflict, not just an absolute-metres one. The built 1.25 m module (vs Argo's 1.28 m) inverts the ~1.4x-wider sibling relationship the ratios describe; counts win per the ring, and the losing ratios stay on the record for a future drawing to referee.
